title: Most people think the fire on Sodom was only about sex.
paragraphs: Most people think the fire on Sodom was only about sex.
It wasn’t.
That city was blazing long before sulfur ever fell.

Ezekiel exposes the real indictment: pride, excess, prosperous ease, and neglect of the poor and needy. Then came abomination. Sin there was not one spark. It was a furnace. “This was the guilt of your sister Sodom…” (Ezekiel 16:49–50).
That matters.
Because we love to condemn the obvious sins of Sodom while baptizing the quieter ones in our own lives.

Comfort without compassion.
Wealth without mercy.
Pleasure without repentance.
Religion without trembling.

And here’s what many miss: the fire that fell on Sodom was not random rage. It was holy judgment on a people who had fully handed themselves over to rebellion. Genesis 19 shows the eruption. Ezekiel shows the roots.
But here’s where grace walks in.

Before the fire fell, God sent warning.
Before destruction, God sent messengers.
Before judgment, God made a way of escape for Lot.
That is the Gospel pattern.
God is not eager to destroy sinners. He warns them. He calls them. He makes a way. And that way is not morality. Not self-reform. Not public image.
That way is Jesus.
On the cross, Christ took the judgment sin deserves so that all who repent and believe in Him will not perish, but be rescued. Sodom is a warning, yes. But Calvary is the rescue.
So don’t just ask, “How wicked was Sodom?”

Ask this instead:
What sins have I normalized because they look respectable?

Pride?
Indifference?
Secret lust?
Hard-heartedness?
A life so full of self there is no room left for God?
The fire on Sodom is not just about what God hates.
It is about how urgently we need mercy.
And mercy has a name.
Jesus Christ.
Let repentance be real, and let grace be louder than your shame.
